meta.title: The Tortoise in the Backpack
meta.textType: story: the theme and the parts

paragraphs: On Wednesday, May and Pat walked home from school. Pat carried a big backpack, and it was very heavy. Near the school wall, he saw something small in the grass. "Look, May! It is a tortoise!" said Pat. It was a little tortoise with mud on its shell. It did not run away, and it did not hide. Pat smiled, and he took it in his two hands.

"I want to keep it," said Pat. "I will put it in my backpack, and we will take it home." "Be careful," said May. Pat put his sweater in the bag first, and then the tortoise. The little creature looked afraid, so they walked slowly. At home, they put it on a towel in the garden. "It is very dirty," said Pat. "I will wash it with shampoo." "No!" said May. "If you use shampoo, the tortoise will be ill."

May brought a small bowl of water. Pat washed the shell with a little water, and the mud came off. "Is the tortoise hungry?" asked Pat. "Let us see," said May, and she gave it a green leaf of lettuce. The tortoise ate it slowly. "Lettuce is tasty for a tortoise," said May. "Even I like it, and I do not like vegetables!" said Pat. "Now the tortoise is my friend." "But a tortoise cannot live in a house," said May. "It is a wild animal, and its home is outside."

Pat looked at the tortoise for a long time. "Its family probably lives near the school wall," said May. "If we keep it, they will not find it." Pat did not say anything. Finally, he said quietly, "Yes, you are right." "We can take it back now." He put the tortoise in the backpack again. Then the two children walked back to the school wall.

Pat put the tortoise on the grass in the same place. For a moment, it did not move. Then it walked slowly under a big leaf. "Goodbye, tortoise," said Pat. "Tomorrow I will say hello again, but I will not take you home." "You did a good thing," said May. Pat smiled at his sister. Sometimes the best way to love an animal is to let it go home.
text.summary: Pat finds a little tortoise near the school wall and takes it home in his backpack. May knows that a wild animal needs its home, and Pat takes the tortoise back.
